ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p439#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p439#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p439#2/r13.claim: The address to humankind means the species collectively received every sort of thing people might request and benefit from, though no individual has all blessings; they are distributed among people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p439#2/r13.anchor: والخطاب للجنس من البشر أي: أن الإنسان قد أوتي من كل ما شأن أن يسأل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك والحسن ومحمد بن علي وجعفر بن محمد وعمرو بن قائد وقتادة وسلام ويعقوب ونافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r1.claim: They read min kull with nunation, meaning from every one of the created things just mentioned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس، والضحاك، والحسن، ومحمد بن علي، وجعفر بن محمد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r2.claim: On one reading mā is relative and a second object: everything that can be requested for benefit; another takes mā as negative and min kull as the second object, meaning blessings people never requested.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r2.anchor: وما موصولة مفعول ثان أي: ما شأنه أن يسأل بمعنى يطلب الانتفاع به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r3.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r3.claim: They give the negative mā interpretation, which reports God's abundant gifts that people did not ask for; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls it al-Ḍaḥḥāk's explanation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r3.anchor: وهذا القول بدأ به الزمخشري، وثنى به ابن عطية وقال: إنه تفسير الضحاك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r4.claim: That negative reading conflicts with the common genitive reading min kulli mā saʾaltumūhu, which instead says people asked; al-Zamakhsharī resolves this by taking the request as need expressed by the state of things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r4.anchor: وهذا التفسير يظهر أنه مناف لقراءة الجمهور من كل ما سألتموه بالإضافة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r5.claim: Mā may also be infinitival; the pronoun in saʾaltumūhu then refers to God, while on a relative reading it refers to the requested thing and its omitted relative link cannot be restored in either proposed form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r5.anchor: والضمير في سألتموه إن كانت ما مصدرية عائد على الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r6.speaker: الواحدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r6.claim: He explains niʿma as a noun used in place of the verbal noun inʿām, so it is not pluralized because it functions as a verbal noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r6.anchor: قال الواحدي: اسم أقيم مقام المصدر، يقال: أنعم إنعاما ونعمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r7.claim: Niʿma apparently means the bestowed blessing, a collective generic noun rather than one blessing; iḥṣāʾ means to enumerate or encompass, and detailed counting is beyond people and known only to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r7.anchor: والذي يظهر أن النعمة هو المنعم به، وأنه هو اسم جنس لا يراد به الواحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r8.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r8.claim: He says a person who sees God's blessing only in food and drink has little knowledge and faces punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p440/r8.anchor: من لم ير نعمة الله عليه إلا في مطعمه ومشربه فقد قل علمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r1.claim: Ibrāhīm ends by calling the human unjust and ungrateful because the preceding verses condemn exchanging God's blessing for disbelief and setting up rivals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r1.anchor: تقدم قوله: ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمت الله كفرا وبعده، وجعلوا لله أندادا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r3.claim: The different endings suit giver and recipient: God gives and forgives or shows mercy, while humans respond with injustice and ingratitude; God may forgive their wrong and show mercy for their failures.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r3.anchor: فحصل من المنعم ما يناسبه حالة عطائه وهو الغفران والرحمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r4.claim: He is cited by al-Sakhāwī for saying Ibrāhīm's ending was abrogated by the ending in al-Naḥl; Abū Ḥayyān dismisses the abrogation claim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r4.anchor: ودعوى إن هذه الآية منسوخة بآية النحل لا يلتفت إليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r5.claim: Humankind generically shows injustice by neglecting gratitude and disbelief by denying blessings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r5.anchor: يظلم النعمة بإغفال شكرها، ويكفرها بجحدها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r6.claim: Another explanation calls people unjust in hardship because they complain and despair, and ungrateful in prosperity because they hoard and withhold.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p441/r6.anchor: وقيل: ظلوم في الشدة فيشكو ويجزع، كفار في النعمة يجمع ويمنع

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r5.claim: A key theme is the sharp difference between gratitude and ingratitude for God’s blessings.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r5.anchor: gratitude and ingratitude for God’s Blessings (see vv. 5, 7–8, 28, 32–34, 37)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Verses 28–34 warn Quraysh leaders that they turned God's favors into grounds for disbelief and led their people to Hell; Muslims are urged to pray and give charity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: used God’s favours a means for their disbelief and polytheism and in this way led their people to Hell.

BURSEVI:v4p280/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p280/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p280/r7.claim: God gives some of everything people ask for, as much as He has apportioned; min can mean “some,” while all can mean abundance, as in 17:18 and 6:44.
BURSEVI:v4p280/r7.anchor: وآتيكم من كل ما سألتموه أي : أعطاكم مصلحة لكم بعض جميع ما سألتموه

BURSEVI:v4p280/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p280/r8.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v4p280/r8.claim: Al-Kashifi says God provides whatever people need, whether or not they ask for it.
BURSEVI:v4p280/r8.anchor: وبداد شمارا أزهر ه خواستيد يعني آنه محتاج إليه شمابود خواسته وناخواسته

BURSEVI:v4p280/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p280/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p280/r9.claim: God’s blessings cannot be counted, even roughly, because they are numerous and limitless.
BURSEVI:v4p280/r9.anchor:
{وإن تعدوا نعمت الله} بسؤال وبغيره.
لا تحصوها لا تطيقوا حصرها وعدها ولو إجمالا لكثرتها وعدم نهايتها.

BURSEVI:v4p280/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p280/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p280/r10.claim: The singular definite noun “blessing” can express comprehensiveness; counting originally used pebbles to mark each decade.
BURSEVI:v4p280/r10.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن المفرد يفيد الاستغراق بالإضافة وأصل الإحصاء أن الحساب كان

BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r1.claim: The Persian couplet says gratitude is the key to increased blessing; one seeking the treasure must not lose that key.
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r1.anchor:
شكر باشد كليد كنج مزيد
كنج خوهى منه ز دست كليد

BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r2.claim: Inwardly, heavens are hearts, earth is souls, rain is wisdom, and its fruits are acts of obedience that nourish spirits.
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r2.anchor: الله الذي خلق السموات سموات القلوب والأرض أرض النفوس وانزل من السماء من سماء القلوب ماء ماء الحكمة

BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r6.claim: Being given what one asks signifies an original readiness to receive divine effusion; God then grants means to rise from the lowest state to the highest.
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r6.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه تعالى أعطى الإنسان في الأزل حسن استعداد استدعى منه لقبول الفيض الإلهي

BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r7.claim: The world was created to support human perfection as a tree is for its fruit; the complete realized human is the fruit of the cosmos.
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r7.anchor: العالم بما فيه خلق تبعا لوجود الإنسان وسببا لكماليته كما أن الشجرة خلقت تبعا لوجود الثمرة

BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r8.claim: Blessings include created things and endless divine tenderness; a person wrongs himself by corrupting this readiness through turning from truth to falsehood.
BURSEVI:v4p280#3/r8.anchor: إن الإنسان لظلوم لنفسه بأن يفسد هذا الاستعداد الكامل بالاعراض عن الحق

QASHANI:14:32-34/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:32-34/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:32-34/r3.claim: God gives each being the perfection it asks through its preparedness, without delay, as also stated in 55:29.
QASHANI:14:32-34/r3.anchor: بألسنة استعداداتكم، فإن كل شيء يسأله بلسان استعداده كمالا يفيض عليه مع السؤال بلا تخلف وتراخ

QASHANI:14:32-34/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:32-34/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:32-34/r4.claim: Blessings before existence and later nurture from the Lordly presence are infinite and cannot be counted.
QASHANI:14:32-34/r4.anchor: من الأمور السابقة على وجودكم الفائضة من الحضرة الإلهية ومن اللاحقة بكم من امداد التربية الواصلة عن الحضرة الربوبية

QASHANI:14:32-34/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:32-34/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:32-34/r5.claim: People wrong themselves by placing innate light and lasting potential in perishing nature or nullifying preparedness, and are ungrateful by misusing blessings and becoming veiled from their giver.
QASHANI:14:32-34/r5.anchor: بوضع نور الاستعداد ومادة البقاء في ظلمة الطبيعة ومحل الفناء وصرفه فيها

QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r3.claim: God gives beyond what people aspire to, ask for, or expect, as the promise to answer supplication confirms.
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r3.anchor: أنلناكم فوق ما تؤملون ، وأعطيناكم أكثر مما ترجون

QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r4.claim: Some reciters read every as nunated and what as a negation, meaning God gave things people never asked for.
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r4.anchor: فينون قوله : كل ويجعل ما سألتموه ( ما ) للنفي

QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r5.claim: The community received gifts before asking through obedience and forgiveness before seeking it through repentance; God knew sinners might be too ashamed to ask.
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r5.anchor: أعطيتكم قبل أن تسألوني - وهذا لأرباب الطاعات ، وغفرت لكم قبل أن تستغفروني

QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r6.claim: God grants forgiveness before the sinner asks, sparing him the shame of recounting his lapses.

QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r7.claim: No servant could have known before existence what God would prepare for him in gnosis, worship, or sin; a poem says love came before awareness and found an empty heart.
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r7.anchor: قبل أن كان له إمكان ، أو معرفة وإحسان ، أو طاعة أو عصيان

QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r8.claim: Human gratitude is too slight to repay abundant blessings, which neither knowledge nor understanding can enumerate.
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r8.anchor: وشكركم نزر يسير ، وإنعامه وافر غزير

QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r9.claim: Protection from trials and disasters is also a blessing, so favors cannot be counted any more than benefits can be counted.
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r9.anchor: فكيف يأتي الحصر والإحصار على ما لا يتناهى

QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r10.claim: The ability to thank God is itself a blessing; each act of gratitude needs further enabling, leaving no end to the favors owed.
QUSHAYRI:v2p125/r10.anchor: إن التوفيق للشكر من جملة ما ينعم به الحق على العبد

SULAMI:v1p346#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r1.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r1.claim: God gave the greatest treasure, unity, without being asked, so the servant should ask and desire only Him and return only to Him.
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r1.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ : إن الله تعالى أعطاك أكثر ما في خزائنه وأجله وأعظمه من غير سؤال

SULAMI:v1p346#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r2.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r2.claim: One diverted from God is cut off from reality, while one absorbed in Him finds created things made compliant and reaches the gnostic's station.
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r2.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ : إن الله تعالى أعطاك أكثر ما في خزائنه وأجله وأعظمه من غير سؤال وهو التوحيد

SULAMI:v1p346#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r3.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r3.claim: One cannot count even a single blessing from its Giver, much less an unbroken succession of blessings.
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r3.anchor: تعد نعمة من المنعم ، فتعجز عن الإحصاء فكيف إذا تتابعت

SULAMI:v1p346#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r4.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r4.claim: Among the greatest blessings are a sound form, inspired knowledge, and remembrance that distinguishes humans from other animals; no one can fully give thanks for them.
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r4.anchor: قيل - أجل النعم استواء الخلقة والهام المعرفة والذكر من سائر الحيوان

SULAMI:v1p346#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r5.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r5.claim: The human wrongs himself by supposing that his gratitude could repay God's blessings, and is ungrateful when veiled from seeing grace at both beginning and end.
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r5.anchor: وقيل : إن الإنسان لظلوم : لنفسه حيث ظن أن شكره يقابل نعمه ، كفار

SULAMI:v1p346#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r6.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r6.claim: God's blessing of Muhammad cannot be enumerated; God made him an intermediary between people and the highest envoy.
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r6.anchor: قال سهل : إن تعدوا نعمة الله : عليكم بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لن تحصوها

SULAMI:v1p346#3/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r7.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r7.claim: The greatest blessing is recognizing blessings and seeing one's own shortfall in thanking their Giver.
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أجل النعم رؤية معرفة النعم ، ورؤية التقصير

SULAMI:v1p346#3/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r8.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r8.claim: Because blessing is eternal, its thanks should be eternal; each faculty has its own blessing, including obedience, fear, certainty, wisdom, love, remembrance, and closeness.
SULAMI:v1p346#3/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : النعمة أزلية كذلك يجب أن يكون شكرها أزلي واعلم أن لك نفسا وروحا وقلبا

TUSTARI:14:34/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:14:34/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:14:34/r1.claim: God's blessings cannot be counted, including His making the greatest messenger and intermediary between people and Himself.
TUSTARI:14:34/r1.anchor: بأن جعل السفير فيما بينكم وبينه الأعلى والواسطة الكبرى

AKHFASH:v2p408/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p408/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p408/r1.claim: وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه means he gave you something of everything requested, with شيء understood after كل.
AKHFASH:v2p408/r1.anchor: وقال {وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه} اي: آتاكم من كل شيء سألتموه شيئا" وأضمر الشيء

AKHFASH:v2p408/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p408/r2.speaker: some
AKHFASH:v2p408/r2.claim: Some interpret من كل as an expression of abundance or generality, as in 'he knows everything' or 'all people came' meaning many or some.
AKHFASH:v2p408/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم: "إنما ذا على التكثير" نحو قولك: "هو يعلم كل شيء" و"أتاه كل الناس" وهو يعني بعضهم:

AKHFASH:v2p408/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p408/r3.speaker: some
AKHFASH:v2p408/r3.claim: Others say people asked for different things, and each received some of what was asked; no single recipient received every request.
AKHFASH:v2p408/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: "ليس من شيء إلا وقد سأله بعض الناس فقال {وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه} أي: "من كل ما سألتموه قد آتى بعضكم منه شيئا وآتى آخر شيئا مما قد سأل".

AKHFASH:v2p408/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p408/r4.speaker: some
AKHFASH:v2p408/r4.claim: Some add tanwīn to كل, meaning 'from every sort' without a specific item requested, as in سألتك من كل and جاءني من كل.
AKHFASH:v2p408/r4.anchor: ونون بضعهم {من كل} يقول {من كل} ثم قال "لم تسألوه إياه"

NAHHAS:v2p370/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p370/r3.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v2p370/r3.claim: Al-Farra interprets من كل ما سألتموه as giving each person what they request, including what they would ask if they had asked.
NAHHAS:v2p370/r3.anchor: فمذهب الفراء من كل سؤالكم كما تقول أنا أعطيته سؤاله وإن لم يسأل شيئا

NAHHAS:v2p370/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p370/r4.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v2p370/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash says God gave something of all they asked for; the phrase can also indicate abundance, as in أوتيت من كل شيء.
NAHHAS:v2p370/r4.anchor: وقال الأخفش وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه شيئا ومثله أوتيت من كل شيء

NAHHAS:v2p370/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p370/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p370/r5.claim: A fourth view says people asked for different things in different circumstances, and the address reflects that variety.
NAHHAS:v2p370/r5.anchor: وفيه قول رابع وهو أن الناس قد سألوا على تفرق أحوالهم الأشياء فخوطبوا على ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r1.claim: The statement that God's blessings cannot be counted reinforces and broadens the preceding conclusion: many blessings are known, and many cannot be comprehended or are forgotten when people try to count them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r1.anchor: تنبيها على أن ما آتاهم الله كثير منه معلوم وكثير منه لا يحيطون بعلمه أو لا يتذكرونه عند إرادة تعداد النعم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r2.claim: Counting means attempting enumeration; familiar but overlooked blessings include breathing, senses, digestion, circulation, and health. Ibn al-Fakhr has a valuable discussion on this point.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r2.anchor: وذلك مثل النعم المعتاد بها التي ينسى الناس أنها من النعم ، كنعمة التنفس ، ونعمة الحواس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r3.claim: Ihsa means accurately fixing a number and derives from pebbles, which people once used to count large totals without error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r3.anchor:
والإحصاء : ضبط العدد
 ، وهو مشتق من الحصا اسما للعدد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r4.claim: The closing assertion reinforces the rebuke of turning blessings into disbelief; human here means the polytheist, as elsewhere in the Quran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r4.anchor: صنف منه ، وهو المتصف بمضمون الجملة المؤكدة وتأكيدها ، فالإنسان هو المشرك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r5.claim: The intensive forms reflect the abundance of blessings and corresponding ingratitude: idolaters abandon worship of the giver for powerless objects, whereas believers acknowledge God's gifts and worship no other.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p236/r5.anchor: إذ بمقدار كثرة النعم يكثر كفر الكافرين بها إذ أعرضوا عن عبادة المنعم وعبدوا ما لا يغني عنهم شيئا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p339/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p339/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p339/r10.claim: The gifts are addressed to humankind collectively: every kind of useful thing that people could ask for has been given, though blessings are distributed among individuals.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p339/r10.anchor: وقوله: وآتاكم للجنس من البشر، أي إن الإنسان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p339/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p339/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p339/r11.claim: An alternate paraphrase says God gave people everything they would have asked for if they had asked.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p339/r11.anchor: وقيل المعنى: وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r1.claim: The author says the alternative reading of God's gifts is close to his preceding collective interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا قريب من الأول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r2.claim: In mā saʾaltumūhu, mā can be a verbal noun with the pronoun referring to God, or a relative pronoun with the pronoun referring to what was given.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r2.anchor: وما في قوله: ما سألتموه يصح أن تكون مصدرية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r3.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم والحسن وقتادة وسلام
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r3.claim: They read kull with tanwīn, as is also reported from Nāfiʿ; the gifts then refer to useful things among the created things previously named.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r3.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك بن مزاحم «من كل ما سألتموه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r4.claim: On that reading, mā is the second object of ātākum; some instead take it as negative, a construal the passage attributes to al-Dahhak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r4.anchor: ف ما في قوله: ما سألتموه مفعول ثان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r5.claim: With the first reading, where kull is annexed to mā, a second object must be supplied, such as a part or thing.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r6.claim: God's blessings are too numerous to count, including senses, capacities, creation after nonexistence, and guidance to faith.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r6.anchor: لكثرتها وعظمها في الحواس والقوى والإيجاد بعد العدم والهداية للإيمان وغير ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r7.speaker: طلق بن حبيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r7.claim: God's due is too weighty for servants to fulfill and His blessings too many to enumerate, so people should end morning and evening repentant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r7.anchor: وقال طلق بن حبيب: إن حق الله تعالى أثقل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r8.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r8.claim: Whoever sees God's blessings only in food and drink has little knowledge and faces punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r8.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء: من لم ير نعمة الله عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r9.claim: Al-insān means the human kind, in which injustice and ingratitude appear in different forms: one in a denier and another in a sinful believer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340/r9.anchor: وقوله: إن الإنسان يريد به النوع والجنس المعنى:

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and ʿIkrima read “from all you asked” literally as all the things you requested.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r1.anchor: أن المعنى من كل الذي سألتموه قاله الحسن وعكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r2.claim: Al-Farra says it means everything you would ask for, even hypothetically.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r2.anchor: من كل ما سألتموه لو سألتوه قاله الفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r3.speaker: الأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies an omitted “something”: God gave you something of everything you asked for, as in 27:23.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r3.anchor: وآتاكم من كل شيء سألتموه شيئا فأضمر الشيء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the wording also includes blessings not requested—such as the sun and moon—by mentioning what was asked and letting it imply what was not, as at 16:81.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r4.anchor: وما لم تسألوه لأنكم لم تسألوا شمسا ولا قمرا ولا كثيرا من النعم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r5.claim: On a reading with tanwin and no possessive construction, Qatada and al-Dahhak say the phrase means God gave you what you did not ask for.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p364#3/r5.anchor: من كل ما بالتنوين من غير إضافة فالمعنى آتاكم من كل ما لم تسألوه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r1.claim: Niʿmat Allah means God’s benefaction, too abundant for anyone to enumerate exhaustively.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ وإن تعدوا نعمة الله ﴾ أي إنعامه ﴿ لا تحصوها ﴾ لا تطيقوا الإتيان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies “the human” as Abu Jahl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس يريد أبا جهل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says “the human” is grammatically the species but refers specifically to the unbeliever.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r3.anchor: الإنسان اسم للجنس يقصد به الكافر خاصة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r4.claim: Ẓalūm means one who wrongs by failing to thank the benefactor; kaffār means one who denies God’s blessings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365/r4.anchor: الظلوم هاهنا الشاكر غير من أنعم عليه والكفار الجحود لنعم الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r1.claim: God prepared everything people need in all circumstances, whether requested by their condition or words; some early authorities include what people ask for and what they do not.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r1.anchor: يقول: هيأ لكم كل ما تحتاجون إليه في جميع أحوالكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r2.speaker: بعض السلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r2.claim: God gives people everything they ask for and what they do not ask for.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r2.anchor: من كل ما سألتموه وما لم تسألوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r3.claim: One reading has أتاكم rather than آتاكم.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم: "وأتاكم من كل ما سألتموه"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r4.claim: People cannot count God's blessings, much less fulfill their duty of thanks; Ṭalq ibn Ḥabīb says God's due exceeds human ability and His blessings exceed counting, so believers should repent morning and evening.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r5.claim: The Prophet praised God as the Lord who needs no provision or replacement and from whom none can dispense; the report is in al-Bukhārī.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r5.anchor: لك الحمد غير مكفي ولا مودع، ولا مستغنى عنه ربنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r6.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r6.claim: A rare, weak-chain report pictures three ledgers at Resurrection: deeds, sins, and blessings; a single blessing consumes all good deeds before God forgives and grants His mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r6.anchor: غريب، وسنده ضعيف. وقد روي في الأثر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r7.speaker: داود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r7.claim: David asks how he can thank God when the very ability to thank is itself a gift; God says that recognizing the inability to repay blessings is now gratitude.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r7.anchor: الآن شكرتني يا داود، أي: حين اعترفت بالتقصير عن أداء شكر النعم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r8.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r8.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says every act of thanking one blessing requires a new blessing, for which one must again give thanks.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r8.anchor: الحمد لله الذي لا يؤدى شكر نعمة من نعمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r9.speaker: القائل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r9.claim: A poet says that even if every limb had a tongue to praise God for His gifts, such praise would still not increase the poet's gratitude enough.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p511#2/r9.anchor: لو كل جارحة مني لها لغة … تثني عليك بما أوليت من حسن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512/r1.speaker: القائل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512/r1.claim: The poem continues that even gratitude expressed through every limb cannot adequately match God's beneficence and gifts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512/r1.anchor: لكان ما زاد شكري إذ شكرت به … إليك أبلغ في الإحسان والمنن

JISHUMI:v5p3873/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3873/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3873/r1.claim: The passage warns against diverting God's blessings into disobedience and neglecting gratitude; worldly enjoyment ending in eternal fire is blameworthy, while contentment with little that leads to Paradise is praised.
JISHUMI:v5p3873/r1.anchor: وتدل على أن المتمتع بالدنيا على وجه يعقب نار الأبد مذموم

JISHUMI:v5p3873/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3873/r3.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وسلام وزيد عن يعقوب
JISHUMI:v5p3873/r3.claim: The common reading annexes ‘from all that you asked’; these readers put tanwīn on kull, allowing the sense that God gave unrequested things or gave each kind in the amount requested.
JISHUMI:v5p3873/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والضحاك وسلام وزيد عن يعقوب: من كل بالتنوين

JISHUMI:v5p3873/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3873/r4.speaker: الضحاك
JISHUMI:v5p3873/r4.claim: With tanwīn, al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God gave things people neither asked for nor imagined.
JISHUMI:v5p3873/r4.anchor: فأما الحجة فقال الضحاك: أي أعطاكم أشياء ما سألتموها

JISHUMI:v5p3873/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3873/r5.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v5p3873/r5.claim: Another view says God gave all that was asked; alternatively He first bestowed gifts without being asked and also granted requested blessings.
JISHUMI:v5p3873/r5.anchor: وقيل في (آتاكم) على هذه القراءة يحتمل وجهين

JISHUMI:v5p3878/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r1.speaker: الأخفش
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r1.claim: The phrase is glossed as God having given people something of everything they need.

JISHUMI:v5p3878/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r2.claim: One explanation is that someone among people has asked for each kind of thing, so God gave from what they asked.
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r2.anchor: ليس شيء إلا وقد سأله بعض الناس، فقال تعالى

JISHUMI:v5p3878/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r3.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r3.claim: An alternative says God gave people things they never asked Him for.
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r3.anchor: أعطاكم ما لم تسألوه، عن الضحاك، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v5p3878/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r4.claim: The objection that some requests go unanswered is answered by the partitive min: God grants according to what is beneficial and in its proper time.
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r4.anchor: لذلك أدخل (من) وهي للتبعيض فيعطي بحسب المصلحة

JISHUMI:v5p3878/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r5.claim: Only the informed petitioner who asks for what is beneficial counts; an ignorant person's request need not be considered.
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r5.anchor: إنما المعتبر بسؤال العارف الذي يسأل بشرط المصلحة

JISHUMI:v5p3878/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r6.claim: God's blessings cannot be counted because they are numerous and include visible and unknown benefits: bodily, provision, worldly, religious, and averting calamities.
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r6.anchor: لأن أنواع النعم في بدنه ورزقه ومنافعه دنيا ثم منافع الدين

JISHUMI:v5p3878/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r7.claim: The verse establishes God as benefactor and thus the one deserving worship; “human” here means disbelievers rather than humanity universally.
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r7.anchor: فبين أنه المنعم وأنه المستحق للعبادة لكن الإنسان مع هذا

JISHUMI:v5p3878/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r8.claim: One gloss calls the disbeliever unjust to himself through ingratitude toward his Lord and consequent deserving of punishment.
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r8.anchor: ظلوم لنفسه بما كفر من نعم ربه واستوجب العقاب

JISHUMI:v5p3878/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r9.claim: Another gloss calls him unjust to blessings because he attributes them to someone other than their originator, and intensely ungrateful.
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r9.anchor: ظلوم للنعم حيث أضافها إلى غير مبتدئها كفار مبالغة في الكفر

JISHUMI:v5p3878/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r10.claim: A third interpretation contrasts injustice in hardship with ingratitude in prosperity.
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r10.anchor: ظلوم في الشدة، كفار في النعمة

JISHUMI:v5p3878/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r11.claim: The legal implication is that believers should hasten to obedience, including establishing prayer and giving alms.
JISHUMI:v5p3878/r11.anchor: تدل الآية على وجوب المبادرة إلى الطاعات من إقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r1.claim: God is the subject and ‘who created’ its predicate; min al-thamarāt clarifies provision or is the object of ‘brought forth,’ with rizqan circumstantial or verbal noun.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r1.anchor: { الله } مبتدأ ، و { الذى خلق } خبره ، و { من الثمرات } بيان للرزق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r4.claim: Min is partitive: God granted some of everything requested, with human interests in view.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r4.anchor: من للتبعيض ، أي آتاكم بعض جميع ما سألتموه ، نظرا في مصالحكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r5.claim: With tanwīn on kull, mā may be negative, yielding gifts unsought; alternatively it is relative and means necessities, as if requested by need.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r5.anchor: وقرىء : ( من كل ) بالتنوين ، وما سألتموه نفي ومحله النصب على الحال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r6.claim: You cannot encompass or count God’s blessings; only God can know them in detail.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r6.anchor: لا تحصروها ولا تطيقوا عدها وبلوغ آخرها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r7.claim: Humans wrong blessings through ingratitude; alternatively, they complain in hardship and hoard in prosperity. ‘Human’ refers to the species.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523/r7.anchor: { لظلوم } يظلم النعمة بإغفال شكرها { كفار } شديد الكفران لها . وقيل ظلوم في الشدة يشكو

MUJAHID:v1p335#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p335#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p335#4/r1.claim: God has granted people everything they have sought from Him.
MUJAHID:v1p335#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه ﴾ يقول كل ما رغبتم إليه فيه

MUQATIL:14:34/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:34/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:34/r1.claim: God granted people unasked gifts out of mercy among the blessings already mentioned; people wrong themselves through sins and are ungrateful for blessings because they do not worship Him.
MUQATIL:14:34/r1.anchor: ما لم تسألوه ولا طلبتموه، ولكن أعطيتكم من رحمتي،

MUQATIL:14:34/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:34/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
MUQATIL:14:34/r2.claim: Abu Salih says the reading with min means God gave things they did not ask for; a reading without min means He answered their requests.
MUQATIL:14:34/r2.anchor: سمعت أبا صالح في قوله عز وجل: { من كل ما سألتموه } ، قال: أعطاكم ما لم تسألوه،

NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r1.claim: Min may be partitive, meaning God gave some of everything requested; alternatively, He gave all requested and unrequested things.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r1.anchor: من للتبعيض أي آتاكم بعض جميع ما سألتموه أو وآتاكم من كل شيء سألتموه وما لم تسألوه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads ما سألتموه as a negation in a circumstantial clause: God granted all those things although people did not ask.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r2.anchor: عن أبي عمرو وما سألتموه نفى ومحله النصب على الحال أي آتاكم من جميع ذلك غير سائليه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r3.claim: Alternatively, ما is relative: God gave what people needed as if they had asked or requested it implicitly.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r3.anchor: أو ما موصولة أي وآتاكم من كل ذلك ما احتجتم إليه فكأنكم سألتموه أو طلبتموه بلسان الحال

NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r4.claim: People cannot count or reach the end of God's blessings, even if they count them generally; only God knows them in detail.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r4.anchor: لا تطيقوا عدها وبلوغ آخرها هذا إذا أرادوا أن يعدوها على الاجمال وأما التفصيل فلا يعلمه إلا الله

NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r5.claim: A person is unjust to a blessing by neglecting gratitude and intensely ungrateful; another reading is that hardship makes one complain while comfort makes one hoard and withhold.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r5.anchor: ﴿ إن الإنسان لظلوم ﴾ يظلم النعمة باغفال شكرها ﴿ كفار ﴾ شديد الكفران لها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r6.claim: Al-insān is generic, applying to anyone in whom injustice and ingratitude are found.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p231#6/r6.anchor: والإنسان للجنس فيتناول الأخبار بالظلم والكفران من يوجدان منه

QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r5.claim: One reading of “He gave you of all you asked” means He granted something from everything requested, with an ellipsis according to al-Akhfash.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r5.anchor: أي أعطاكم من كل مسؤول سألتموه شيئا فحذف عن الأخفش

QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r6.claim: Another explanation says God gave what people asked for and also what they never asked for—such as the sun, moon, and many blessings He initiated; a third regards “min” as extra and reads that He gave everything requested.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r6.anchor: ومن كل ما لم تسألوه فحذف، فلم نسأله

QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Dahhak, and others read “wa-atākum min kulli” with a tanwin on “kull”; this reading is reported also from Hasan and Qatada and is interpreted negatively, as referring to what was not asked for, such as sun and moon. Another parsing takes “ma” as a relative pronoun.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والضحاك وغيرهما { وءاتكم من كل }

QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r8.claim: The blessings of God are too numerous to count or encompass, including hearing, sight, the shaping of bodies, health, and provision.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r8.anchor: { لا تحصوها } ولا تطيقوا عدها، ولا تقوموا بحصرها

QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r9.claim: Since these blessings come from God, people should not exchange them for disbelief but should use them to obey Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r9.anchor: وهذه النعم من الله، فلم تبدلون نعمة الله بالكفر؟

QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the human as Abu Jahl.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أراد أبا جهل.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:32-34/r11.claim: Another interpretation takes “the human” as the generic category but intends all disbelievers.

RAZI-FULL:v19p99#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p99#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p99#2/r1.claim: After describing the saved and damned, the author concludes with proofs of the Creator, whose knowledge is the chief source of happiness and whose absence is misery.
RAZI-FULL:v19p99#2/r1.anchor: العمدة العظمى والمنزلة الكبرى في حصول السعادات معرفة الله تعالى بذاته وبصفاته

RAZI-FULL:v19p99#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p99#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p99#2/r2.claim: The passage contains ten signs: creating the heavens and earth, sending rain and producing provisions, subjecting ships and rivers, setting the sun and moon in motion, and granting what people ask.
RAZI-FULL:v19p99#2/r2.anchor: وذكر ههنا عشرة أنواع من الدلائل . أولها : خلق السموات . وثانيها : خلق الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v19p99#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p99#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p99#2/r3.claim: These proofs and their interpretation have been discussed repeatedly earlier in the work; the author adds a few further observations here.
RAZI-FULL:v19p99#2/r3.anchor: وهذه الدلائل العشرة قد مر ذكرها في هذا الكتاب وتقريرها وتفسيرها مرارا وأطوارا

SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r1.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r1.claim: For the common reading, he takes من as extra in the second object, yielding وآتاكم كل ما سألتموه.
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنها زائدة في المفعول الثاني، أي: كل ما سألمتموه، وهذا إنما يتأتى على قول الأخفش

SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r2.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r2.claim: He treats من as partitive: God gave some of all they asked for, with an omitted object, considering their interests and needs.
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r2.anchor: والثاني: أن تكون تبعيضية، أي: آتاكم بعض جميع ما سالتموه نظرا لكم ولمصالحكم

SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r3.claim: ما may be a relative pronoun, a verbal noun particle, or an indefinite noun with an adjective; the verbal noun can stand for the requested thing.
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r3.anchor: و " ما " يجوز فيها أن تكون موصولة اسمية أو حرفية أو نكرة موصوفة، والمصدر واقع موقع المفعول

SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r4.claim: If ما is a verbal noun particle, its pronoun refers to God; if relative or adjectival, it refers to the requested thing and its resumptive pronoun cannot be omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r4.anchor: فإن كانت مصدرية فالضمير في " سألتموه " عائد على الله تعالى، وإن كانت موصولة أو موصوفة

SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and the listed authorities read من كل with tanwin; ما may then be negative and a circumstantial phrase meaning God gave freely without your asking.
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومحمد بن علي وجعفر بن محمد والحسن والضحاك

SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r6.claim: He first takes ما in the tanwin reading as negative, with the sense that the gifts arrived without being requested.
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r6.anchor: وفي " ما " على هذه القراءة وجهان، أحدهما: أنها نافية، وبه بدأ الزمخشري فقال: " وما سألتموه نفي

SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r7.claim: He prefers taking ما as a relative pronoun and the second object of آتاكم because it better aligns the tanwin reading with the common reading.
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r7.anchor: والثاني: أنها موصولة بمعنى الذي، هي المفعول الثاني لآتاكم. وهذا التخريج الثاني أولى

SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r8.claim: To address the apparent mismatch, he allows ما to be relative and paraphrases asked as what people needed, as though they requested it by their state.
SAMIN-DURR:14:34/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون " ما " موصولة على: وآتاكم من كل ذلك ما احتجتم إليه، ولم تصلح أحوالكم

SAMIN-DURR:14:34#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:34#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:34#2/r1.claim: نعمة here means the thing bestowed, and the ending with الإنسان لظلوم is apt after the preceding account of replacing God's blessing with disbelief and assigning Him partners.
SAMIN-DURR:14:34#2/r1.anchor:
نعمة " في معنى المنعم به، وختمت هذه ب { إن الإنسان لظلوم } ، ونظيرتها في النحل ب
إن الله لغفور رحيم

SAMIN-DURR:14:34#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:34#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:34#2/r2.claim: The Nahl ending differs because that passage details blessings and contrasts the Creator with what cannot create, so divine forgiveness and mercy fit its emphasis.
SAMIN-DURR:14:34#2/r2.anchor:
والتي في النحل ذكر فيها عدة تفصيلات وبالغ فيها، وذكر قوله
أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق

RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r7.claim: The omitted object in “He gave you of all you asked” is estimated as a portion of every requested thing; God gave far more benefits than can be counted.
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r7.anchor: والمفعول محذوف تقديره من كل مسؤول شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r8.claim: One reading gives kullin tanwīn and treats mā as negation in a circumstantial accusative: God gave from everything without their asking.
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r8.anchor: وقرىء : { من كل } بالتنوين و { ما سألتموه } نفي ومحله نصب على الحال

RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r9.claim: Alternatively, mā is relative: God supplied everything people needed for sound life and livelihood, as though they had asked by their state.
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ( ما ) موصولة والتقدير : آتاكم من كل ذلك ما احتجتم إليه

RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r10.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r10.claim: Niʿma is a noun used in place of the verbal noun inʿām, so it is not pluralized because it carries a collective verbal sense.
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r10.anchor: قال الواحدي : النعمة ههنا اسم أقيم مقام المصدر

RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r11.claim: “You cannot enumerate them” means people cannot count all God’s blessings because of their abundance.
RAZI-FULL:v19p101#2/r11.anchor: أي لا تقدرون على تعديد جميعها لكثرتها

RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r1.claim: Studying the nerves shows why blessings cannot be enumerated: cranial and spinal nerves branch into countless delicate pathways, each with a specific function whose disruption harms the body.
RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r1.anchor: أن الأعصاب قسمان ، منها دماغية ومنها نخاعية . أما الدماغية فإنها سبعة

RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r2.claim: Each tiny nerve branch is a great blessing, and humans cannot inspect its condition or enumerate its benefit; the same applies to arteries, veins, and every organ.
RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r2.anchor: عرف أن الله تعالى بحسب كل شظية من تلك الشظايا العصبية على العبد نعمة عظيمة

RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r3.claim: The same inexhaustible complexity extends from the body to the soul, animals, celestial spheres, elements, land, sea, plants, and creatures.
RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r3.anchor: فاعرف أقسام نعم الله تعالى في نفسه وروحه ، فإن عجائب عالم الأرواح أكثر من عجائب عالم الأجساد

RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r4.claim: Even all created intellects combined could discern only a little of divine wisdom in the smallest things.
RAZI-FULL:v19p102/r4.anchor: أن عقول جميع الخلائق لو ركبت وجعلت عقلا واحدا ثم بذلك العقل يتأمل الإنسان في عجائب حكمة الله تعالى في أقل الأشياء لما أدرك منها إلا القليل

RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r1.claim: Understanding even one bite of bread requires the whole world’s order: wheat depends on seasons, elements, weather, and celestial motions, while its tools depend on iron and prior tools.
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r1.anchor: لأن الحنطة لا بد منها ، وأنها لا تنبت إلا معونة الفصول الأربعة ، وتركيب الطبائع

RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r2.claim: Understanding what follows a bite requires anatomy and medicine, since one must know how the body uses food and where eating can harm it.
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r2.anchor: فتأمل في تركيب بدن الحيوان ، وهو أنه تعالى كيف خلق الأبدان حتى يمكنها الانتفاع بتلك اللقمة

RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r3.claim: These dependencies prove that even one blessing cannot be fully understood, confirming that blessings cannot be enumerated.
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r3.anchor: فظهر بهذا البرهان القاهر صحة قوله تعالى : { وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها }

RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r4.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r4.claim: The human is unjust by neglecting gratitude for blessings and intensely ungrateful by denying them.
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r4.anchor: قيل : يظلم النعمة بإغفال شكرها كفار شديد الكفران لها

RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r5.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation says people complain and despair in hardship, then hoard and withhold during prosperity; “the human” denotes the species’ customary behavior.
RAZI-FULL:v19p102#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : ظلوم في الشدة يشكو ويجزع ، كفار في النعمة يجمع ويمنع

RAZI-FULL:v19p103/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p103/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p103/r1.claim: Because people forget or tire of blessings, they neglect gratitude; if they reflect on some blessings, they overlook others.
RAZI-FULL:v19p103/r1.anchor: فإذا وجد نعمة نسيها في الحال وظلمها بترك شكرها ، وإن لم ينسها فإنه في الحال يملها

RAZI-FULL:v19p103/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p103/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p103/r2.claim: The contrast with 16:18 presents humans as unjust and ungrateful in receiving blessings, while God is forgiving and merciful in giving them.
RAZI-FULL:v19p103/r2.anchor: فأنت الذي أخذتها وأنا الذي أعطيتها ، فحصل لك عند أخذها وصفان

RAZI-FULL:v19p103/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p103/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p103/r3.claim: God’s forgiveness and mercy mean that human failure is answered with further provision and harshness with faithful generosity.
RAZI-FULL:v19p103/r3.anchor: إن كنت ظلوما فأنا غفور ، وإن كنت كفارا فأنا رحيم

STUDYQURAN:14:34/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r1.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r1.claim: God gives people some of what they ask verbally or what they request implicitly through need without speaking.
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r1.anchor: God gives people something of all that they ask for with their tongues, or of what they ask for by being in a state of need without actually articulating it verbally (Bḍ)

STUDYQURAN:14:34/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r2.claim: Because mā can be read differently, some understand the verse to say God gives unrequested blessings such as the sun and moon.
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r2.anchor: some read this to mean, “He gives you of that which you do not ask of Him,” referring to blessings such as the sun and the moon (Q)

STUDYQURAN:14:34/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r3.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r3.claim: Legitimate requests, excluding sin or severed family ties, are answered by granting them now, storing the reward for the Hereafter, or diverting an equivalent evil.
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r3.anchor: The Prophet is reported to have said that God will grant one’s legitimate requests

STUDYQURAN:14:34/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r4.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r4.claim: People cannot count God's blessings or thank Him for all of them.
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r4.anchor: they are also unable to thank Him for all of them (Bg; see also 16:18)

STUDYQURAN:14:34/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r5.claim: The description of humanity as ungrateful is echoed in many verses and complements the description of humanity as an ignorant wrongdoer.
STUDYQURAN:14:34/r5.anchor: Truly mankind is wrongdoing, ungrateful is complemented by the last part of 33:72

TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r1.claim: God has supplied some of what people ask and desire; the object is omitted because the partitive من already indicates that only some of each requested thing is meant.
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r1.anchor: وحذف الشيء الثاني اكتفاء بما التي أضيفت إليها «كل» ، وإنما جاز حذفه، لأن «من» تبعض ما بعدها،

TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r2.claim: Alternative explanations take كل as rhetorical hyperbole for many things or people, or say that different people received different things they requested.
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r2.anchor: وقد قيل: إن ذلك إنما قيل على التكثير، نحو قول القائل: فلان يعلم كل شيء، وأتاه كل الناس،

TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r3.claim: A Basran grammarian understands the wording as granting what each person asked for; a Kufan grammarian takes it to include everything one might request even without asking.
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r3.anchor: وهذا قول بعض نحويي أهل البصرة. وكان بعض نحويي أهل الكوفة يقول: معناه: وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه لو سألتموه،

TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r4.claim: Mujahid interprets the wording as granting whatever people sought and desired from God.
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {من كل ما سألتموه} [إبراهيم: 34] ورغبتم إليه فيه.

TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r5.claim: Hasan glosses it as granting all that you asked for.
TAB-FULL:v13p682#2/r5.anchor: عن معمر، عن الحسن: {وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه} [إبراهيم: 34] قال: «من كل الذي سألتموه» .

TAB-FULL:v13p684/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p684/r1.speaker: ركانة بن هاشم
TAB-FULL:v13p684/r1.claim: Rukanah ibn Hashim reports the interpretation that God gave both what people asked for and what they did not ask for.
TAB-FULL:v13p684/r1.anchor: عن داود بن أبي هند، عن ركانة بن هاشم: {من كل ما سألتموه} [إبراهيم: 34] وقال: ما سألتموه وما لم تسألوه "

TAB-FULL:v13p684/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p684/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v13p684/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak reads كل with tanwin and no annexation to ما, interpreting it as unrequested gifts such as the sun, moon, night, and day.
TAB-FULL:v13p684/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم، في هذه الآية: {وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه} [إبراهيم: 34] ، قال: ما لم تسألوه

TAB-FULL:v13p684/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p684/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p684/r3.claim: Qatada says God gave people what they had not requested among the things He granted.
TAB-FULL:v13p684/r3.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة: «وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه» قال: «لم تسألوه من كل الذي آتاكم»

TAB-FULL:v13p684/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p684/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p684/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the standard recitation annexing كل to ما: God granted some things people asked for, as the authoritative reciters agree, and rejects the alternative reading.
TAB-FULL:v13p684/r4.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندنا، القراءة التي عليها قراء الأمصار، وذلك إضافة «كل» إلى «ما»

TAB-FULL:v13p686/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p686/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p686/r1.claim: People cannot enumerate God’s blessings or fulfill gratitude unaided; the unjust and ungrateful person redirects worship from the benefactor and abandons His obedience.
TAB-FULL:v13p686/r1.anchor: الذي بدل نعمة الله كفرا لظلوم: يقول: لشاكر غير من أنعم عليه، فهو بذلك من فعله واضع الشكر في غير موضعه،

TAB-FULL:v13p686/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p686/r2.speaker: طلق بن حبيب
TAB-FULL:v13p686/r2.claim: Talq says God’s due is too weighty to fulfill and His blessings too numerous to count, so people should end each day repentant.
TAB-FULL:v13p686/r2.anchor: قال: «إن حق الله أثقل من أن تقوم به العباد، وإن نعم الله أكثر من أن تحصيها العباد، ولكن أصبحوا توابين وأمسوا توابين»

ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r1.claim: الإنسان is a generic noun here but specifically denotes the unbeliever, as in the passage that excludes believers from humanity’s loss.
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r1.anchor: هذا اسم للجنس يقصد به الكافر خاصة، كما قال: (والعصر (1) إن الإنسان لفي خسر (2) إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات).

TABATABAI:14:32-34/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:32-34/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:32-34/r7.claim: Questioning is a request addressed to a rational being, unlike the broader category of requesting; need prompted people to express requests verbally, though signs and writing also count literally as questions.
TABATABAI:14:32-34/r7.anchor: السؤال هو الطلب ويفارقه أن السؤال إنما يكون ممن يعقل

TABATABAI:14:32-34/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:32-34/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:32-34/r8.claim: Every created being depends on God's generosity for existence and continuance, so all beings are inherently asking God to meet their needs whether or not they acknowledge Him or receive every requested thing.
TABATABAI:14:32-34/r8.anchor: كان كل من سواه عاكفا على باب جوده سائلا يسأله رفع ما حلت به من حاجة

TABATABAI:14:34/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:34/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:34/r1.claim: Intrinsic asking is directed only to God; verbal requests may be addressed to God or other people, but the verse's unrestricted giving shows that every need of humanity as a species is met wholly or partly.
TABATABAI:14:34/r1.anchor: هذا هو حق السؤال وحقيقته يختص به تعالى لا يتعداه إلى غيره

TABATABAI:14:34/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:34/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:34/r2.claim: The species' requests are genuine and directed only to its Lord, so all are answered; individual people may make insincere or misdirected prayers, which explains why a particular person's request can go unmet.
TABATABAI:14:34/r2.anchor: فجميع أدعيته مستجابة وسؤالاته مؤتاة وحاجاته مقضية

TABATABAI:14:34/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:34/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:34/r3.claim: The preposition min means that God's gifts are drawn from what people asked for, sometimes wholly and sometimes partly according to wisdom; a partitive reading would wrongly imply every request is only partly granted.
TABATABAI:14:34/r3.anchor: ابتدائية تفيد أن الذي يؤتيه الله مأخوذ مما سألوه

TABATABAI:14:34/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:34/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:34/r4.claim: Reading the phrase as giving both what people ask for and what they do not ask for relies on verbal asking, which Tabataba'i has rejected and finds unsupported by the context.
TABATABAI:14:34/r4.anchor: وما لم تسألوه وهو مبني على كون المراد بالسؤال هو السؤال اللفظي

TABATABAI:14:34#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:34#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:34#2/r1.claim: The interdependent universe and its effects are blessings benefiting one another, beyond enumeration; the singular blessing names the whole genus and conveys abundance without a plural.
TABATABAI:14:34#2/r1.anchor: فالجميع نعمه بالنسبة إلى الجميع وهذا أمر لا يحيط به إحصاء

TABATABAI:14:34#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:34#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:34#2/r2.claim: Humanity is intensely unjust and ungrateful: people wrong themselves by failing to thank God, or wrong God's blessings by denying them; this explanatory comment follows from human heedlessness of those blessings.
TABATABAI:14:34#2/r2.anchor: أي كثير الكفران يظلم نفسه فلا يشكر نعمة الله

TABATABAI:14:19-34#18/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:19-34#18/r8.speaker: علي بن الحسين
TABATABAI:14:19-34#18/r8.claim: Al-Kafi reports that when al-Sajjad recited the verse on counting blessings, he praised God for making recognition of blessings consist in admitting one's inability to know them, and treating that admission as gratitude.
TABATABAI:14:19-34#18/r8.anchor: عن علي بن محمد عن بعض أصحابه رفعه قال كان على بن الحسين عليه السلام

TABRISI:14:32-34/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:32-34/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:32-34/r6.claim: God grants many requests, including health, safety, wealth, children, honor, ease, and comfort, unless granting them would harm religion or another person.
TABRISI:14:32-34/r6.anchor: يسأل الله العافية فيعطى ويسأله النجاة فيعطى ويسأله الغنى فيعطى

TABRISI:14:32-34/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:32-34/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:32-34/r7.claim: The partitive min is necessary: saying God grants every request would be false because harmful requests are withheld; the sense is that He grants something from each kind requested.
TABRISI:14:32-34/r7.anchor: ودخلت من للتبعيض لأنه لو قال وآتاكم كل ما سألتموه لاقتضى أن جميع ما يسأله العبد يعطيه الله تعالى

TABRISI:14:32-34/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:32-34/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:32-34/r8.claim: An alternative says God has supplied whatever people need among themselves, as in His statement that He created everything on earth for them.
TABRISI:14:32-34/r8.anchor: فما من شيء يحتاج إليه العباد إلا وهو موجود فيما بينهم

TABRISI:14:34/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:34/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:34/r1.claim: Niʿma is a singular noun used in place of a verbal noun, so it is not pluralized; this shows God is the true benefactor and deserves worship.
TABRISI:14:34/r1.anchor: والنعمة هنا اسم أقيم مقام المصدر ولذلك لم يجمع فبين سبحانه أنه هو المنعم على الحقيقة

TABRISI:14:34/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:34/r2.speaker: طليق بن حبيب
TABRISI:14:34/r2.claim: God's claim is too weighty for servants to fulfill and His blessings too numerous to count, so they should begin and end each day repentant.
TABRISI:14:34/r2.anchor: إن حق الله تعالى أثقل من أن يقوم به العباد فإن نعم الله أكثر من أن تحصيها العباد

TABRISI:14:34/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:34/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:34/r3.claim: Ẓalūm means greatly wronging oneself, while kaffār means repeatedly showing ingratitude for one's Lord's blessings.

TABRISI:14:34/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:34/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:34/r4.claim: An alternative describes people as complaining in hardship and hoarding and withholding during prosperity; the verse's human is a particular type, as in the Sūrat al-ʿAṣr passage, not all humanity.
TABRISI:14:34/r4.anchor: ظلوم في الشدة يشكو ويجزع كفار في النعمة يجمع يمنع ولم يرد بالإنسان ها هنا العموم

TABRISI:14:34/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:34/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:34/r6.claim: This verse follows the mention of people setting up rivals: the one truly entitled to divinity and worship is God, creator of the heavens and earth.
TABRISI:14:34/r6.anchor: لما ذكر ما هم عليه من اتخاذ الأنداد لله سبحانه بين بعده أن واجب الوجود المستحق للإلهية

TABRISI:14:34/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:34/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:34/r7.claim: Another reading takes ma as an indefinite relative and supplies an omitted clause: God gave what people asked for and what they did not ask for; the omitted sense is supported by the clothing verse.
TABRISI:14:34/r7.anchor: فما ها هنا نكرة موصوفة والجملة صفة له وحذف الجملة المعطوفة

THALABI:v5p320/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p320/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p320/r3.claim: ‘He gave you of all you asked’ may omit a second شيء: you receive something from each category requested; another reading treats ‘all’ as general abundance rather than literal totality.
THALABI:v5p320/r3.anchor: وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه يعني وآتاكم من كل شيء سألتموه شيئا

THALABI:v5p320/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p320/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p320/r4.claim: Another interpretation says God granted both what people asked for and what they never asked for; the common reading attaches ما سألتموه in an إضافة construction.
THALABI:v5p320/r4.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: معناه وآتاه من كل ما سألتموه وما لم تسألوه

THALABI:v5p320/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p320/r5.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v5p320/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says God gave people things they did not request or even imagine, as the speaker can attest.
THALABI:v5p320/r5.anchor: قال الضحاك: أعطاكم أشياء ما طلبتموها ولا سألتموها

THALABI:v5p320/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p320/r6.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وسلام
THALABI:v5p320/r6.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, and Salam read من كل with nunation, construing the phrase as provision from what people had not asked for.
THALABI:v5p320/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والضحاك وسلام: من كل، بالتنوين على النفي

THALABI:v5p320/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p320/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p320/r7.claim: People cannot enumerate God’s blessings or fulfill their thanks for them by heart, tongue, or explanation.
THALABI:v5p320/r7.anchor: ولا القيام بشركها لا بالجنان ولا باللسان ولا بالبيان

THALABI:v5p320/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p320/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p320/r8.claim: The human is unjust by failing to thank a benefactor and placing gratitude wrongly, and ungrateful by denying God’s blessings; other views tie injustice to disobedience or hardship and ingratitude to hoarding in prosperity.
THALABI:v5p320/r8.anchor: إن الإنسان لظلوم لشاكر غير من أنعم عليه واضع الشكر في غير موضعه

ASAD-NOTES:14:34#n47/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:34#n47/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:34#n47/r1.claim: God grants a person’s desires when divine wisdom deems their satisfaction ultimately beneficial; min qualifies the request as receiving something from what was asked.
ASAD-NOTES:14:34#n47/r1.anchor: provided that His unfathomable wisdom regards its satisfaction as ultimately beneficial to the human being concerned

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r1.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r1.claim: The object of “He gave you” is omitted: He gave you something from everything requested, like other verses that omit “something.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r1.anchor: المفعول محذوف تقديره من كل مسؤول شيئا أو مسؤولا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r2.claim: On Abū al-Ḥasan’s grammatical analysis, the prepositional phrase is accusative and min is extra even in an affirmative clause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r2.anchor: أن يكون الجار والمجرور في موضع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r3.claim: God gives what people asked for and what they never requested, such as sun and moon; mentioning requests can stand for unasked gifts, as in the clothing that protects from heat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r3.anchor: وما لم تسألوه؛ لأنا لم نسأله شمسا ولا قمرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري؛ الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r4.claim: Another reading is that God gave whatever people wish, desire, or prefer; al-Kisāʾī notes that asking language can mean getting one’s wish, not literal questioning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p480#2/r4.anchor: وآتاكم من كل ما تتمنون تشتهون وتؤثرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r1.claim: Niʿmat is a verbal noun standing for inʿām, so it remains singular as an infinitive would.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r1.anchor: النعمة هاهنا اسم أقيم مقام المصدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r2.claim: Lā tuḥṣūhā means you cannot count all God’s abundant favors, as 72:28 says He encompasses the number of all things.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r2.anchor: لا يأتوا على جميعها بالعد لكثرتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r3.claim: Lā tuḥṣūhā can mean that people cannot preserve or remember the favors.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r4.speaker: أبو العالية؛ الفراء؛ غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r4.claim: A further gloss is inability to endure or perform the favors; these two readings also occur at 73:20, where al-Farrāʾ interprets it as keeping night-vigil times and others as being unable to bear it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p482/r4.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: لا تطيقون عدها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r1.claim: God’s blessings are His favors, too numerous to count; the human being here means the disbeliever, who wrongs himself and denies his Lord’s favor.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r1.anchor: إنعام الله عليكم { لا تحصوها } لا تطيقوا عدها

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:32/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:32/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:32/r4.claim: People benefit from these gifts throughout life and receive many further material and spiritual blessings; God says He has granted people what they ask, and His blessings cannot be counted.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:32/r4.anchor: O, insana maddî ve mânevî daha nice nimetler bahşetmiştir. Nitekim 34. âyette Allah insanların istediği her şeyi verdiğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:32/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:32/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:32/r5.claim: Despite the duty to thank God at every moment, humanity ignores the giver, is ungrateful, and associates partners with Him; the verse highlights these negative traits.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:32/r5.anchor: nimetleri vereni görmezlikten gelerek nankörlük etmekte, O’na ortak koşmaktadır

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The statement that God gives people what they ask for addresses humanity in its capacity as human beings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The words “and has given you from everything you asked for” address human beings in their capacity of being human beings.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The fit between human demand and provision is strong evidence that the Creator arranged for every human need.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The complete correspondence between demand and supply is the greatest evidence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The author explains that the general wording is used because the idolaters are unworthy of direct address for their conduct.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Since they are not worthy of being addressed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God supplies whatever human nature and physical form need, in keeping with wisdom; the match between needs and provision shows the Creator provides for all needs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: whatever their nature and physical form needs is provided to them by God in accordance with His wisdom and expediency

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Though phrased generally, “human beings” refers here to the idolaters discussed earlier; the general wording reflects their unworthiness because of their conduct.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: it refers to the idolaters which are being discussed since the previous verses.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Ẓalūm describes one who usurps rights; polytheism violates both God's right and the person's own soul.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: When a person indulges in polytheism, he not only usurps the right of God but also of his one soul.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Kaffār means ungrateful: thanking someone other than the one who actually bestowed the favor.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: He is a person who thanks someone other than the one from whom he has received favours.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، الضحاك، محمد بن علي، جعفر بن محمد، عمرو بن فائد، يعقوب
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r1.claim: They read من كل ما سألتموه with tanwin, making the object explicit: God gave what they asked Him to grant from it; the standard genitive construction leaves the object understood as a share from every kind.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r1.anchor: قراءة ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك ومحمد بن علي وجعفر بن محمد

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343/r1.claim: Qatada says God did not give people everything they asked for, since they did not request all that He gave them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه ﴾ قال لم تسألوه كل الذي آتاكم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343/r2.claim: Al-Hasan instead says God gave people everything they asked Him for.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن آتاكم من كل الذي سألتموه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r1.claim: God gave people some of what they asked for, in keeping with His will, wisdom, and benefit; من is partitive in this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r1.anchor: أي أعطاكم بعض جميع ماسألتموه حسبما تقتضيه مشيئته التابعة للحكمة والمصلحة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r2.speaker: بعض الكاملين
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r2.claim: Some scholars take كل to intensify abundance rather than assert exhaustive coverage, as in the cited wording about every door being opened to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعض الكاملين : إن ( كل ) للتكثير والتفخيم لا للإحاطة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r3.claim: Partitive من does not make كل redundant: both the range of kinds and all members within each kind matter, while human need concerns a kind of thing rather than each individual instance.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r3.anchor: فالمعنى أعطاكم من جميع أفراد كل صنف سألتموه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r4.claim: سألتموه includes what people need by their condition, whether expressly requested or not; need counts as a request in the language of circumstance, as in the primordial covenant exchange.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r4.anchor: وفسر ( ماسألتموه ) بما من شأنه أن يسأل لاحتياج الناس اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r5.claim: Another account restores an omitted phrase, and God gave you what you asked and what you did not ask, the latter understood from the retained wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : الاصل وآتاكم من كل ماسألتموه وما لم تسألوه فحذف الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that if ما is a relative pronoun and its pronoun refers back to it, the proposed antecedent construction would require two same-rank pronouns together or an impermissibly omitted attached pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r6.anchor: ومنع أبو حيان جواز أن يكون راجعا اليه تعالى ويكون العائد على الموصول محذوفا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r7.claim: Others allow those pronoun analyses, arguing that the ban on two same-rank pronouns applies when both appear, and that omitting a detached pronoun is permissible when omission serves a grammatical rather than emphatic purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r7.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى جواز كلا التقديرين مدعيا أن منع اتصال المتحدين رتبة خاص

ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r8.claim: ما may also be a relative, a descriptive noun, or a verbal noun, in the last case meaning what was requested; the pronoun is then understood as referring to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون موصوفة والكلام في الضمير كما تقدم وأن تكون مصدرية

ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p225#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
